title: [Feature][KV Pool] Prefetch layerwise loads on a global layer window
body:
## What this PR does / why we need it?

Layerwise pooling prefetches a layer's pool load `layerwise_prefetch_layers` (`P`) model layers ahead of the layer that consumes it. Its window was written for the layout where every rank owns every layer: the cursor that decides which layers may be submitted advanced by *local* submissions - it walked the layer cursor and stopped after `P` successful submissions, skipping the layers this rank does not own.

KVPP changes that layout: a rank owns only a contiguous share of the layers. Keeping the same prefetch schedule on the owner-sharded layout means the window has to advance in model-layer units instead of counting local submissions. Counting local submissions has two consequences:

1. **The window did not follow the model layers under KVPP.** A rank owning a late shard skipped every layer before its partition and submitted its whole partition during the first model layers, so those loads were issued at the front of the forward instead of at model layer `max(0, L - P)`.
2. **The configured prefetch distance was not honored.** After the first model layer the loop submitted exactly one layer per model layer, so `load(L)` was issued at model layer `L-1` regardless of `layerwise_prefetch_layers`; `P` was only effective at layer 0.

This PR adapts the window to the owner-sharded layout by expressing it in model-layer units: `window_end = min(current_layer + P, num_layers - 1)`. `load(L)` is then submitted at model layer `max(0, L - P)`, which is the schedule `layerwise_prefetch_layers` describes. Layers a rank does not own are still skipped inside `submit_layer_load()`, and `block_key_hybrid` already used this window, so its separate count is removed.

This PR also carries the layer index fix that KVPP + layerwise pooling needs to run on main at all:

- Layerwise transfer tasks carry a group-local layer index that indexes the per-group address tables (`group_layer_cache_entry_offsets`). Under KVPP those tables are built from the layers this rank registered, while the map that produced the index was built from the full model layer list. Every rank that does not own the first shard then looks past the registered entries:

  ```text
  IndexError: index 10 is out of bounds for axis 0 with size 10
    at kv_transfer.py build_addrs -> self._layer_cache_entry_offsets_np[layer_id + 1]
  ```

- Rebuilding that map from the owner-filtered layer list keeps the index owner-relative (`0..registered-1`), consistent with the address tables, `group_num_layers` and `final_group_layer`; layers this rank does not own produce no group entry, which is what the transfer loop expects.

## Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

The layer-to-owner mapping, the KVPP broadcast and the loaded data are unchanged; only the model layer at which a layerwise load is submitted now follows `layerwise_prefetch_layers`. The documentation lists Mooncake layerwise pooling as supported with KVPP (it previously stated the opposite) and documents `use_layerwise=true` with `load_async=false`.

## How was this patch tested?

- New unit test `test_layerwise_prefetch_window_advances_with_model_layer` in `tests/ut/distributed/ascend_store/test_pool_worker.py`. It pins the model layer at which each owned layer is submitted for a full partition, a first shard and a late shard, with `P = 2`. It fails on the previous loop: a late shard (`[5, 6, 7]`) was submitted at model layers `0, 0, 1` instead of `3, 4, 5`.
- `python -m pytest -q tests/ut/distributed/ascend_store/test_pool_worker.py`
- Local check of the index change: simulating the address tables and both index sources (78 layers, 8 ranks, single group and two groups) yields 0 out-of-bounds lookups after the change versus 68 before it.
- End-to-end on GLM-5.2, TP8, Model Runner V2 with `--enforce-eager`, `AscendStoreConnector` with `backend="mooncake"`, `use_layerwise=true`, `load_async=false`: the pool load of layer `L` was observed to complete before its KVPP broadcast and `load_ready` never timed out. That run used a separate opt-in instrumentation build, which is not part of this PR.

### End-to-end measurements (GLM-5.2)

Measured TTFT (mean over 128 requests) in three configurations. All three rows come from the same instance, the same workload and the same service settings in one test batch; only `enable_kvpp` and `use_layerwise` differ. The last row is the configuration this PR concerns.

| Devices | Model | Input | Output | Prefix hit rate | Deployment | Concurrency | Requests | TTFT (ms) | KVPP | Layerwise |
| ---: | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | :---: | :---: |
| 8 | GLM-5.2-W4A8C8 | 128K | 1 | 90% | P/D mixed, TP8 | 32 | 128 | 132.8 | Yes | No |
| 8 | GLM-5.2-W4A8C8 | 128K | 1 | 90% | P/D mixed, TP8 | 32 | 128 | 125.6 | No | Yes |
| 8 | GLM-5.2-W4A8C8 | 128K | 1 | 90% | P/D mixed, TP8 | 32 | 128 | 135.6 | Yes | Yes |

The third row is higher because two per-layer effects stack and are not fully hidden behind compute:

1. **The KVPP broadcast is already the dominant per-layer cost, and most of it stays exposed.** Measured on the same configuration with an opt-in instrumentation build (not part of this PR): one layer broadcasts about 2 GiB (`num_blocks=14216`) in ~98 ms on the device (~22 GB/s), while the compute window of that layer is only ~4.3 ms, so attention waits ~103 ms per layer and the broadcast is on the critical path. This cost exists with KVPP alone as well.
2. **Layerwise pooling adds one pool load per layer with almost no slack, on the same interconnect.** It requires `load_async=false`, so each owner rank issues one H2D per layer during the forward (~22-50 ms per layer, ~10 layers per rank) instead of a single bulk asynchronous load. That traffic shares the interconnect with the broadcast, and the load has to complete before its layer runs: the measured margin is ~1 ms, so any extra delay caused by that sharing is exposed instead of being absorbed by compute.

Combining these two mechanisms leaves part of their cost uncovered, which is what the +2.8 ms (+2.1%) over the KVPP-only row reflects; without KVPP (second row) there is no per-layer broadcast to compete with, and without layerwise the pool load is one bulk asynchronous transfer.
